criteria.criterion: In athena.toml, the [[capabilities.change.checks]] entries named fmt and clippy each have skip_when_only = ["docs/", "*.md"], and no other patterns.
criteria.evidence: `git diff HEAD~1 -- athena.toml` shows `skip_when_only = ["docs/", "*.md"]` added under fmt and under clippy and nowhere else. The new test `skip_when_only_is_set_on_fmt_and_clippy_only` checks this exact list and passes.

criteria.criterion: The change capability's test check has no skip_when_only key, and athena.toml has a comment explaining why: xtask/tests/policy.rs reads docs/*.md and scans every tracked file, so a prose change can fail a test.
criteria.evidence: The diff adds no key to the test check. It adds this comment above the test check: "The test check never skips. xtask/tests/policy.rs reads docs/*.md, and its boundary scan reads every tracked file, .md files included, so a prose change can fail a test." The test asserts `skip("test") == None`.

criteria.criterion: The [capabilities.study] checks and every other athena.toml key are unchanged.
criteria.evidence: The athena.toml diff has one hunk with additions only: two skip_when_only lines and three comment lines inside the change capability's checks. No other line changes.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md under Unreleased says the key is now enabled for fmt and clippy only, and the earlier 'does not set the key' follow-up wording no longer reads as pending.
criteria.evidence: The diff removes "This change does not set the key ... enabling it is a separate follow-up job". It adds "`athena.toml` now sets the key on the change capability's fmt and clippy checks only, with `docs/` and `*.md` ... The test check never skips ..."

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`; all pass. The repository's config tests load athena.toml, so this shows it still parses.
criteria.evidence: `cargo test --locked`: every suite reports ok with 0 failed, including config::tests::repository_config_parses_and_validates, both skip_when_only tests, and the 9 xtask policy tests. `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` finished with no warnings. `cargo fmt --all --check` exited cleanly with no output.

findings.summary: crates/athena-data/src/config.rs changed, but it is not a listed deliverable.
findings.evidence: The old test asserted that REPO_CONFIG has no skip_when_only key, so it would fail once the key is set. Changing it was needed. The new test pins the configured lists, and the old parsing test now targets the test check. This is a needed, in-scope test update, but the reading did not predict it.

findings.summary: The athena.toml comment says fmt and clippy "read no prose", but several crates compile .md prompt files with include_str!.
findings.evidence: Grep finds include_str!("../prompts/*.md") in athena-context, athena-cap-study and athena-cap-change. Editing those files cannot change fmt or clippy results. Deleting or renaming one would break the build, but the test check never skips and compiles everything, so it still catches that. The skip is safe; only the comment is slightly imprecise.

summary: The change does what you asked. In athena.toml, the fmt and clippy checks for code changes now skip any change made only of files under docs/ or .md files. The test check still runs on every change, and a comment says why: the xtask policy tests read docs/*.md, and their file scan reads every tracked file, .md files included, so a prose-only change can still fail a test. The study capability's checks and every other key are unchanged. The CHANGELOG and row M31 of docs/enforcement.md now say the skip is turned on, instead of calling it a pending follow-up. The change also updates a test in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs, which is not on the deliverables list. That update was needed, because the old test checked that athena.toml had no skip key. The new test pins the exact skip lists for all three checks. I ran `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`, and all three passed. I found two minor issues: the extra config.rs file, and a comment saying fmt and clippy "read no prose", although some crates build .md prompt files into the code with include_str!. The skip is still safe, because the test check always builds the code.
